claims.claim: Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU that runs interaction nets in hardware after agents handled the full flow from theory to 7 nm GDS.
claims.episode_span: Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU that runs interaction nets in hardware.
claims.source_title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI
claims.supporting_quote: Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU that runs interaction nets in hardware. Agents took it from theory to 7 nm GDS, and pre-silicon tests show 4.59x performance per watt over an in-order core.

claims.claim: Pre-silicon tests show 4.59x performance per watt versus a conventional in-order core on the same workload class.
claims.episode_span: Pre-silicon tests show 4.59x performance per watt versus a conventional in-order core on the same workload class.
claims.source_title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI
claims.supporting_quote: pre-silicon tests show 4.59x performance per watt over an in-order core

claims.claim: The new component re-implements division via log-exp and stabilizes deeper CoFrGeNets without incremental training; on GPT-2, Llama-3, Mamba-2 and nano-MoE it matches or exceeds prior continued-fraction work with higher tokens per second.
claims.episode_span: The new component re-implements division via log-exp and stabilizes deeper CoFrGeNets without incremental training; on GPT-2, Llama-3, Mamba-2 and nano-MoE it matches or exceeds prior continued-fraction work with higher tokens per second.
claims.supporting_quote: re-implementation of divisions makes training of deeper CoFrGeNets stable without the need for incremental training

claims.claim: Across six open models, recall of self-generated hallucinations that receive outcome-based rewards rises 4.83% on average while unrewarded hallucinations rise only 0.17%; backtracking templates inherited from reasoning training further entrench false facts that the model later retracts.
claims.episode_span: Across six open models, recall of self-generated hallucinations that receive outcome-based rewards rises 4.83 % on average while unrewarded hallucinations rise only 0.17 %; backtracking templates inherited from reasoning training further entrench false facts that the model later retracts.
claims.supporting_quote: recall of hallucinations reinforced during training increases by 4.83% on average, compared to just 0.17% for self-hallucinations that receive no training signal

claims.claim: Native coordinate axes align better with other models, human brain responses, and interpretable linguistic features than random rotations that preserve geometry, yet still fall short of optimal alignment.
claims.episode_span: Native coordinate axes align better with other models, human brain responses, and interpretable linguistic features than random rotations that preserve geometry, yet still fall short of optimal alignment.
claims.supporting_quote: native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes

claims.claim: Starting from benchmark trajectories it builds executable tests, validates them against reference solutions, then generates new tasks that isolate suspected causes; human annotators accept 90% of the resulting failure-mode descriptions and reject 83.3% of similar alternatives.
claims.episode_span: Starting from benchmark trajectories it builds executable tests, validates them against reference solutions, then generates new tasks that isolate suspected causes; human annotators accept 90 % of the resulting failure-mode descriptions and reject 83.3 % of similar alternatives.
claims.supporting_quote: annotators accept 90.0% of assigned descriptions and correctly reject 83.3% of similar alternatives

claims.claim: On 20 Twitter IO campaigns the resulting detector reduces missed detections of adaptive agents by 65% relative to a detector trained only on archived campaigns while holding false-alarm rate constant; engagement-seeking agents become easier to catch after training.
claims.episode_span: On 20 Twitter IO campaigns the resulting detector reduces missed detections of adaptive agents by 65 % relative to a detector trained only on archived campaigns while holding false-alarm rate constant; engagement-seeking agents become easier to catch after training.
claims.supporting_quote: this detector reduces missed detections of adaptive agents by 65% relative to a detector trained only on the archived campaigns, at a similar false-alarm rate

claims.claim: Across eight LLMs and 12 000 episodes they adopt planted procedural errors in only 2.9% of rulings yet follow majority generic reviews up to 71% of the time and drop witness limitations up to 65% of cited claims; obligation prompts reduce but do not eliminate the failures.
claims.episode_span: Across eight LLMs and 12 000 episodes they adopt planted procedural errors in only 2.9 % of rulings yet follow majority generic reviews up to 71 % of the time and drop witness limitations up to 65 % of cited claims; obligation prompts reduce but do not eliminate the failures.
claims.supporting_quote: senior agents rarely adopt a planted procedural error (2.9% of rulings) but often follow a majority of generic reviews (up to 71% of decisions) or drop witnesses' stated limitations (up to 65% of cited claims)
